<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Esther 8:15">Targ. Esth. VIII, 15</cite> <cite ref="C00156"><he>גַּדָּא</he></cite> (not <cite ref="C00156"><he>גָּדָא</he></cite>).—
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 71:9">Gen. R. s. 71</cite> <he>ג׳ דביתא</he> the good genius of the house.
Sabb. 67ᵇ גד גַּרִּי וסינוק לא (Ms. M. צינוק), a charm formula supposed to mean, Be lucky, my luck, and tire not (prob. Grow, my luck &c., v. נְגַד).
<cite ref="Chullin 40a:3">Ḥull. 40ᵃ</cite> <he>לג׳ דהר</he> to the godhead of the mountain.

<cite ref="Nedarim 56a:6">Ned. 56ᵃ</cite> (explain. <cite ref="D01041"><he>דרגש</he></cite>) <he>ערסא דג׳</he> the bed reserved for the domestic genius (bed of state). Y. Ab. Zar. I, 39ᵈ top <he>לגַרֵּיה וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="A03242"><he>ארקליס</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 65:18">Gen. R. s. 65</cite> <he>ג׳ דע״ז דאת קאים</he> [<cite ref="B00537"><he>ביה</he></cite>] by the idolatrous godhead by whom thou standest, i.e. to whom thou referrest in saying, ‘Let my father rise’ (<cite ref="Genesis 27:31">Gen. XXVII, 31</cite>).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 16:6:1">Y. Sabb. XVI, end, 15ᵈ</cite>; Y. Yoma VIII, 45ᵇ; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 4:9:2">Y. Ned. IV, 38ᵈ</cite> <he>בגַדָּךְ מדלי</he> (not <he>בגרך</he>) doest thou rely upon thy good luck? <cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 7:26:1">Koh. R. to VII, 26</cite> <he>מה ביש ג׳ וכ׳</he> how bad is this woman’s (my) luck!; a. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="C00201"><he>גַּדַּיָּיא</he></cite>, <cite ref="C00195"><he>גַּדַּיָּא</he></cite>.
Y. Ab. Zar. III, 43ᵃ bot. ג׳ קורין אותה גליא a place called Gaddaya is cacophemistically named Gallaya (dung-hills); Tosef. ib. VI (VII), 4 גדגיא ed. Zuck. (ed. גריא, corr. acc.).
